cards.explanation: The answer is that the nations are being prepared to come against Babylon. The command is plain: “Prepare the nations against her.” The banner and the ram's horn are all pointed at one target, friends. Next the passage starts naming who gets called up.

The answer is the kings of the Medes. The passage says, “…the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the lands they rule.” Those kings get prepared for battle alongside the kingdoms named just before. Notice, bakers, that the list reaches past the kings to their officials and the lands they rule.

The answer is True. The passage says, “The earth quakes and writhes because the LORD’s intentions against Babylon stand…” Even the earth feels it when the LORD's intentions stand, friends. I think I'd be shaking right alongside it, and I'm standing on a gold base.

The answer is a desolation without inhabitant. The LORD's intentions are “to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.” That means an empty, ruined land with no one living in it. The verse says it plainly, friends.

The answer is gates. The verse says, “…the bars of her gates are broken.” The warriors are sitting in their strongholds at the same time, bakers. Gate bars are what hold a gate shut, and these ones are broken.

The answer is that his city has been captured from end to end. The messengers come “…to announce to the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end.” The news covers the whole city, friends, not just one corner. And one courier after another keeps coming with it.

The answer is False. The text says the soldiers are terrified. The verse reads, “The fords have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified.” Terrified is about as far from calm as you can get, bakers.

The answer is harvest. The LORD says, “In just a little while her harvest time will come.” A threshing floor is where harvested grain gets worked, friends, so the word fits the picture. And the time He gives is “…just a little while…”

The answer is that he has devoured and crushed her. The speaker says, “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has crushed me.” The next verse has words from the dweller of Zion and from Jerusalem. I think this is a heavy line, friends, and it's okay to let it be heavy.

The answer is on Babylon. The dweller of Zion says, “May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon…” Then Jerusalem says, “May my blood be on the dwellers of Chaldea…” I think these are heavy words, friends.

The answer is that the LORD will plead her case and take vengeance for her. He says, “Behold, I will plead your case and take vengeance on your behalf…” Notice the word "I" in that line, bakers. The LORD says it right after Jerusalem's words.

The answer is rubble. The LORD says, “Babylon will become a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals…” Rubble is what's left of a city after it falls, friends. The verse goes on to say it will be “…an object of horror and scorn, without inhabitant.”

The answer is that they fall asleep and never wake up. The LORD says, “then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, declares the LORD.” The feast comes first, friends, and then the sleep that has no morning. I think this is a heavy line.

The answer is True. The verse says, “The praise of all the earth has been seized. What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!” The verse sets the praise of all the earth right beside the horror Babylon has become, bakers. That's quite a drop.

The answer is False. The verse says, “Her cities have become a desolation, a dry and arid land, a land where no one lives, where no son of man passes through.” Dry and arid is a long way from a green land full of fields, friends. It's dry, and no one lives there.

The answer is that they stop streaming to him. The LORD says, “The nations will no longer stream to him…” Bel is a false god of Babylon, friends, and the crowds that came to him will stop coming. The LORD is the one doing the punishing in this verse.
The answer is False. The verse ends, “even the wall of Babylon will fall.” The word "even" tells you the wall was the kind of thing you'd expect to hold, bakers. But the LORD says it falls too.
